root_idea.summary: The root denotes flowing and extending, especially the movement of water and other fluids.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development includes flowing water, channels through which water runs, causing a substance to flow, abundant flow, and figurative extension or pouring forth. Several specialized nominal and technical uses remain distinct.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form.
Displayed as the nominal citation form سَيْلٌ.

senses.definition: To flow or run, especially of water or a watercourse.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, it is said of valleys as their water flows according to its measure.

senses.definition: To make something flow or run; to cause a liquid or molten substance to flow.
senses.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV. The Quranic occurrence concerns causing molten copper or brass to flow for Solomon.

senses.definition: A torrent or flood: a large body of rainwater flowing through a valley or watercourse.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic contexts use the noun for a torrent or flood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fluid or liquid, opposite to becoming solid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical use describing a thing that becomes fluid, not merely water flowing through a channel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be swept into a difficult or severe situation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative proverbial construction in which a torrent carries people into hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour or descend upon someone in force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction used of horsemen pouring upon a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To extend or spread lengthwise or downward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse's facial blaze and, by comparison, of flowing or defluent hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something long and complete.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV use, especially of the point or blade of an arrow, spear, or similar implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour together or converge from different directions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of troops pouring together from every quarter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flowing or running water when the verbal noun is used adjectivally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the construction مَاءٌ سَيْلٌ, the noun functions in place of an adjective meaning flowing or running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode or manner of flowing or running water.
The tang or tongue of a sword, knife, or similar implement that enters its hilt or handle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This technical noun is distinct from the ordinary meanings of flowing and running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thorny tree or plant, especially a white-thorned acacia-like species.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The botanical identification is variously described in the lexical evidence; سَيَالٌ is also treated in relation to سَيَالَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flowing or running abundantly; distilling much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of water or another liquid that flows or distills copiously.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular mode of calculation.
A bend in a sea or a great river.
Fluid or liquid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing a substance capable of flowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extended or spreading.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In سَائِلُ الأَطْرَافِ it describes extended fingers; in غُرَّةٌ سَائِلَةٌ it describes a facial blaze spreading over the forehead or nose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or group of people pouring in from a direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative collective use for people arriving or moving together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Valleys or watercourses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural use associated with places through which water flows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In مُسَالُ الخَدَّيْنِ, having expanded cheeks; in مُسَالَا الرَّجُلِ, the two sides of a man's beard or jaws, and by extension his two sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional anatomical and descriptive expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or channel in which a torrent or water flows; a watercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word also functions as an infinitive noun in the sense of flowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain that causes much flowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for rain producing abundant flow in valleys or watercourses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain that causes valleys and watercourses to flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun distinct in vocalization from مَسِيلٌ ‘watercourse’.

cautions: The botanical referent of سَيَالٌ is variously identified in the lexical evidence, including acacia-like and other thorny plants.
The sword-tang sense of سِيلَانٌ is recorded with an explicit qualification that the report was heard but not from a learned authority.
The Quran example for أَسَالَ uses the secure QAC location 34:12; historical citation notation in the lexical evidence is not treated as a modern verse locator.
